Documentation → Releases → 3.1.0

SATOM 3.1.0

All five products are now drawn from their own measured GUI, every field only the CLI has is shown and editable, every write is checked on the device, and Naming Discovery finds the convention your devices already follow.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user

Released: 2026-10-13 · All releases

In short#

SATOM 3.1 makes each device ADOM look and behave like the appliance it manages. FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC and now FortiAnalyzer are all drawn from the GUI layouts measured on their exact firmware build, and the old SATOM menus leave those ADOMs. Every field and object the Fortinet GUI does not show is listed under Not in GUI, but in CLI, and can be edited there. Every write SATOM makes is read back from the device and judged: Verified on the device, Not applied or Not verified.

The release also adds Naming Discovery (the naming convention your devices already follow, with one click to adopt it), drawn network diagrams with flow tracing under Fleet → Architecture, and a long list of operator CLI commands. All screens are translated again in German, French, Italian and Spanish. Several security fixes close data that other local accounts, or a forged request, could reach. Read Before you upgrade.

What's new#

Every product drawn from its own measured GUI#

The Knowledge Harvester now crawls the real GUI of each product, and the layouts reach your node through the knowledge feed, one per page and exact build. A new firmware build no longer needs a SATOM release to get its layout. The release itself ships no layout, so a node that has not imported a knowledge pack has none. See Knowledge packs.

  • FortiWeb. Every page with a layout is drawn the way FortiWeb draws it: its menu in its order, its tabs, columns, dialogs, fields and show/hide rules, inside the SATOM frame. Everything shown is editable, with a dry run first. Settings that FortiWeb's GUI saves through its own API (log settings, Admin Settings, FortiGuard) are read and saved the same way. About 20 pages that used to be empty (Signatures, the certificate lists, FortiSandbox, Automation and others) now show and edit their objects.
  • FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator get the same engine. Pages read the device live (FortiAuthenticator from SATOM's copy when it has one) and save through dry run, apply, read-back and audit. Inline table rows, Clone and Create New work. FortiAuthenticator DNS, interfaces and static routes are read and written over the CLI.
  • FortiADC is the fourth product drawn this way. Rows are read live from the REST API, writes follow the same audited path, and child tables (pool members, BFD interfaces, HA monitor lists and so on) are created, edited and deleted under their parent. The FortiView pages appear in the menu as live monitors. The measured Virtual Server list has a Wizard button for the Virtual Server wizard.
  • FortiAnalyzer is the fifth. Its pages read the device live over JSON-RPC get. Writes show the exact JSON-RPC request in a dry run, then send add, update or delete to /cli/global objects only, record the change and re-read the object. Passwords are never shown or sent back. Views the GUI saves through its own private calls are drawn read-only and link to the device. Monitor pages such as FortiView and Log View say "Live monitor" and link to the device.
  • Import safety. Every endpoint in a FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC or FortiAnalyzer layout is now checked against that product's rules on import, as FortiWeb's always were. A layout that names a device action (reboot, upgrade, backup, restore, factory reset and the like) is refused. A layout where only one tab names an action is now imported without that tab, and the import says what was cut.
  • Old menu URLs redirect to the measured page that draws the same objects. Where a classic page still exists, ?classic=1 opens it.

See Not in GUI, but in CLI, FortiAnalyzer, FortiADC, FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator.

Not in GUI, but in CLI, on every product#

SATOM now shows every field a device has on its exact build. Fields the Fortinet GUI does not show are listed in a section titled Not in GUI, but in CLI, and each one says how SATOM writes it: REST (a normal save), CLI (the CLI writer over SSH) or unverified on this build.

  • The section is on every object page, also when it is empty (it then says why).
  • On FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer the section is now an editor for users with write permission. Read values over CLI fills the fields over a read-only SSH session. Preview CLI change shows the exact script. Apply runs it through the CLI writer in one transaction and reads it back.
  • FortiWeb, FortiGate and FortiADC menus gain a Not in GUI, but in CLI group: pages for every object of the build that no page of the device's own GUI edits. On FortiWeb that is 89 objects on 7.6.8 and 124 on 8.0.6.
  • Appliances → device → Not in GUI, but in CLI lists everything a device has outside its GUI. For FortiADC this includes each object's rows, read from the device when the page opens. The device menus of FortiADC, FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator end with an entry for this page.

Every write is checked on the device#

Until now, "ok" meant only that the device accepted the request. Some builds accept a write and silently drop a field.

  • After every accepted write, SATOM re-reads what it touched and compares every field it sent. The result is Verified on the device, Not applied (with the value the device kept, audited as config.<action>.not_applied) or Not verified (with the reason).
  • FortiWeb: a write the device did not keep now fails. This applies in clone, migrate, bulk changes, scheduled actions, the object editor and exception injection. SATOM's copy is updated right after each write, so a change made from SATOM shows at once, without a rediscovery.
  • FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator and FortiADC configuration pages, and the FortiADC writers (certificates, Lua Studio, the decommission, the ADC object editor and its wizard, POST /api/v1/adc/rules), check every create, update and delete the same way. FortiAnalyzer's measured pages re-read each object after a write.
  • API consoles and the /api proxy show the same verdict next to the device's raw reply, without failing.
  • FortiWeb same-box clone now gives the copy its own virtual server and VIP, and refuses before any write a copy FortiWeb would reject. Deleting a policy also deletes the VIP it owns when no other policy uses it.

Naming Discovery: Adopt and Adopt & adapt#

Administrator → Naming is now in every device ADOM. Its new Discovery tab reads the configuration SATOM already holds (no device call). For each object type it shows the pattern your devices follow (for example pol-{adom}-{name}), how many objects follow it, every exception with its reason, and names that no longer match their object.

  • A part of a name becomes a token such as {port} or {proto} only when it equals a field of the object on at least 80 % of the objects. Vendor and factory objects are counted apart and never shape a pattern.
  • The Scheme tab lists the same object types as Discovery, including types no device holds yet, next to the pattern Discovery found (all devices agree / devices differ) and a live count of the names that follow what you type.
  • Adopt writes the discovered pattern into the scheme. Adopt & adapt opens it in an editor first; Save to scheme stores it.
  • Entries SATOM builds new names from (marked builds names) accept {name} only, and Adopt and Save refuse anything else and say why.
  • A fleet view and a formula-safe CSV export are included.

See Naming.

Settings → ADOM Menus#

Settings → User Interface → ADOM Menus replaces Settings → FAZ Menu. It has three switches, each named after a page's banner: Hide live-monitor pages, Hide pages managed on the device and Hide GUI-only pages (no API). Each applies to every ADOM and every user. A page leaves the menu only when all its tabs are of a hidden kind. A direct link still opens it. The panel shows how many pages each switch hides per ADOM. All switches are off by default. See ADOM Menus.

Fleet → Architecture: drawn network diagrams#

A new page, Fleet → Architecture, in every ADOM (Architecture). You draw the path of a service (Internet, LAN, segments and VLANs, every Fortinet product, back-end servers, management hosts) and bind each device element to its SATOM appliance. The cache-based map that used to carry this name is now called Service Diagram (Service Diagram).

  • Read devices reads the bound devices, read-only: FortiGate interfaces and firewall policies with hit counts, and one HTTP probe per back-end with a probe URL. Nothing read is cached.
  • Trace a flow: enter source and destination IP, protocol and port. Each FortiGate on the drawn path answers for itself with its own routing and policy lookup. SATOM never evaluates a rule base. The path is drawn cyan (allowed), red (denied) or amber (unknown). TCP traces through a FortiWeb or FortiADC offer Validate with Scout.
  • Layers L2, L3, L4 and L7, an Elements palette that lists the ADOM's appliances, autosave with undo and redo, and versioned saves: if a colleague saved first, you see their version and yours stays one Undo away.
  • Saving needs configuration write permission and is audited.

API library and harvest: FortiADC, FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer#

  • FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer can now be harvested live like FortiWeb, FortiADC and FortiAuthenticator, by the apilib_harvest scheduled action, on a firmware change, or on demand from Schema builds → Harvest. Both harvests only read. The FortiAnalyzer and FortiADC adapters are now marked verified on Schema builds, so all five products are verified on a real device.
  • FortiADC fields that read REST only or unknown now meet their CLI path, and fields REST and the CLI spell differently (direct_route_ip / direct-route-ip, mkey / the table key) count as one field: on 7.6.7, 967 fields read both instead of 10. On FortiADC, CLI only now means the REST API has no such object at all.
  • A new exception reason, platform, marks FortiGate tables that a VM cannot serve because they are hardware or platform features.
  • FortiAnalyzer fields that read REST only or unknown now meet their CLI path: on 7.6.7, 1,494 fields read both instead of none.
  • The FortiGate ADOM has an API group and an API console. Its endpoint registry is seeded with the 624 cmdb tables of FortiOS 8.0.1. Writes are dry-run by default, reach /api/v2/cmdb/ only, need the "Execute write API calls" permission and are audited.
  • FortiADC rediscovery offers Capture full depth: every child table (REST). The VS Inspector follows each virtual server through every reference: content routing, pools, members, real servers, SSL profiles and certificate chains, auth policies and more. It also reads only what the virtual servers reach (about 0.8 s instead of 7.6 s on 15 virtual servers). From last rediscovery draws the same tree without contacting the device.
  • FortiADC appliances now offer Upgrade and Boot Partition, through the same runbook as FortiWeb, including Boot alternate partition.

See API library, Schema builds and Firmware upgrade.

The operator CLI catches up#

  • satom get device not-in-gui <device>: the per-device "Not in GUI, but in CLI" inventory.
  • satom get device naming [<device>]: Naming Discovery, per device or as the fleet consensus.
  • satom get signatures status: the signature database age of every FortiWeb, judged like the alert.
  • satom show layouts [<product>]: the measured GUI layouts on the node, and whether each device has one for its exact build.
  • satom diagnose data and satom execute repair data --yes: check and fix file permissions under data/ (see Security).
  • satom diagnose config now checks the host rules of password-reset links.
  • satom ha check and satom ha repair [--yes]: see below.
  • satom execute restart-all compiles the language catalogues first when they are older than their source.

See Operator CLI.

Repairing the HA link from the primary#

On a primary, Software Update & HA shows an HA link card: whether the standby is in sync, how many commits behind it is, or since when it cannot fetch code from this node. The Repair HA link button (and satom ha repair) previews first, then restarts systemd-logind on the primary only. A new alert, HA link broken, fires when the standby has failed to fetch for more than 10 minutes. See High availability.

Translations complete again#

All four catalogues now cover every string the interface can show: 6,127 of 6,127 in German, French, Italian and Spanish. About 2,700 strings had been showing in English. A new check fails as soon as a string ships without a translation in one of the four languages, or a translation drops or invents a placeholder. Spanish is still off by default in Settings → Languages; turning it on now gives a complete interface. Offline update packages and rollbacks now recompile the catalogues too. See Languages.

FortiWeb signatures: a source and a local index#

  • Administrator → Signatures → Signature source picks the FortiWeb SATOM collects signatures from; Save and collect now reads its whole catalog.
  • A local signature index keeps every signature with its history (first seen, last seen, removed in) and what each database version added, changed or removed. Administrators are notified of a new version.
  • The signature check now reads database versions over REST, with SSH as the fallback, and names an invalid FortiGuard licence as the reason when it is one.

See Signatures and Signature database freshness.

Templates across firmware builds and devices#

  • Provisioning → Compare templates shows a template against a newer one on a build or a device, with a VALID verdict only when it fits.
  • The compatibility matrix shows every template of the ADOM against every measured or fleet build.
  • Device bindings: a device follows the newest approved version of a template or is pinned to one, with its own values for {{ variable }} placeholders. A device with a missing value is refused.
  • Adapt to firmware lists the fields a newer build adds, and each one must be decided. The upgrade pre-flight checks the templates that govern the device.

See Template library.

Smaller additions#

  • Bookmarks: a star on every left-menu entry adds the page to Favourites; clicking the filled star removes it. See Bookmarks.
  • Server Policy list: Clone, Clone to, Migrate to, Enable, Disable and Delete run on the list itself, on several ticked policies at once. The classic list's filters and clone history moved onto it.
  • Every device ADOM has the same Fleet → WAF, Operations, Automation, Administrator and Plugins entries as FortiWeb. An entry whose page only understands FortiWeb is greyed out and says why on hover. Scout is in the Fleet group of every ADOM.
  • Separate SSH password per appliance (Edit appliance), for FortiAuthenticator, whose SSH refuses the REST API key.
  • FortiGate CPU and memory are now collected.
  • An alert warns when a SATOM process is running code older than what is on disk.

What changes for you#

  • Device ADOMs draw only the device's own menu. The old SATOM menus and the Classic view button are gone from FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator and FortiADC. FortiAnalyzer draws its own menu when a layout exists for its build and keeps the curated menu otherwise.
  • The classic Server Policy list is gone. /web/workspace/<id> opens the Server Policy list.
  • Settings → FAZ Menu is removed, together with its list of hidden entries. Use Settings → ADOM Menus.
  • Menu order is the same in every ADOM. Appliances moved to Administrator; Schema builds, Build compatibility and Certificate Manager moved to Automation; Global Studio joined Administrator; FortiWeb's API is an API group, and the sidebar no longer links Documentation. A profile that cannot see a new group keeps the entry where it was. On FortiWeb, Search Attack ID, Exceptions & Signature and WAF Artifacts moved to Fleet → WAF.
  • A build with no evidence now blocks a template apply. It used to pass as a warning. An approver can still override with a reason, which is audited. A build measured only by its CLI tree warns instead of blocking.
  • Approving a Web Protection Profile template follows its bindings. It deploys only to the bound devices, renders {{ variables }} per device, and holds the whole deploy if a device has no value.
  • Signature collection only uses the configured source. The signature_sync scheduled action refuses any other target.
  • FortiADC Capacity Limits is greyed out, because its catalog counts FortiWeb object types.

Fixed#

  • A FortiGate never had a configuration tree. It is now synced like the other products, with secrets removed. The scheduled Sync device actions offer FortiGate.
  • Hourly sync errors. A FortiADC on 7.6 logged seven HTTP 404 errors per hour for tables only 8.0 serves; a FortiAnalyzer failed on report and log-file endpoints. Both are now left out.
  • Opening a FortiWeb signature profile in the GUI no longer counts as configuration drift. Upgrading does not raise a drift alert for every device either.
  • System Provisioning and baselines render {{ variables }} per device. A literal placeholder used to reach every device. The NTP element now writes the cmdb NTP object instead of FortiWeb's GUI API.
  • Create New Server Policy refuses a policy with no service before anything is written, and a failed run deletes what it created. The form shows its full set of fields on every installation (it showed 11 on all but the first).
  • The Server Policy dialog saves through the same checks as the object editor: template lock, edit lease and build compatibility.
  • FortiAuthenticator CLI writes now work: the CLI writer understands FortiAuthenticator's prompts.
  • The deep-monitor sweep took 12 minutes on a 3-minute schedule; probes that cannot connect no longer stall it, and the network part runs concurrently.
  • A scheduler restart during a run no longer stops that action for an hour: a lease held by a process that has ended on the same node is released at once.
  • Software Update named an old API pack for the release lane when a newer knowledge pack already held its content; it now names the release's pack, "covered by" the newer one.
  • satom get device status reported hourly-synced devices as "never synced", and satom get system health now warns when a service runs code older than the code on disk.
  • A rediscovery with deep or CLI capture no longer looks finished halfway.
  • Phone layout: the menu stopped working after the first navigation (this also affected desktop), the top bar ran off-screen and pages were wider than the screen.
  • The per-device "Not in GUI, but in CLI" page took 60 s on a FortiGate; it now takes about 1 s.
  • The template compatibility matrix took 40-50 s; it now takes about 2 s.
  • The FortiADC VS Inspector never showed the client SSL profile.
  • A FortiAnalyzer's model was stored with the product name twice.

Security#

  • The FortiAnalyzer configuration sync stored device secrets. HA, SQL and backup passwords, certificate passwords and data-mask keys were kept in the stored configuration and in every configuration version. The sync now drops them, as the FortiGate sync already did. Versions recorded before this fix still contain those values.
  • Device configurations and database bundles were readable by other local accounts on the node. data/ is now 0750, system bundles and the device configuration vault are written 0600 in 0700 directories, and the installer and the updater apply the same rule. satom diagnose data checks it.
  • The password-reset link no longer follows a forged Host header. A request with a foreign Host could have mailed a live reset token pointing at another server. The link now keeps the request's host only when it is one of the node's own names or is listed in the new LINK_HOSTS setting. See Configuration files.
  • FortiADC requests that reboot, shut down, factory-reset or swap the boot partition are plain GETs. They are now refused, for every method and permission, and audited in the FortiADC API console, the /api proxy, scheduled custom REST calls and the discovery sweep.
  • The SQL console's CSV export neutralises spreadsheet formulas.
  • System restore extracts only regular files and directories, with a strict containment check.
  • The vault address and the Sentinel model endpoint must be http or https.
  • The CLI support bundle is private from its first byte, and a certificate signer no longer uses /tmp as its home directory.
  • Werkzeug 3.1.9 (CVE-2026-102598; it affects Windows only, so SATOM on Linux was not exploitable).

Before you upgrade#

  • Database changes are applied for you. The updater runs the four new migrations (architecture diagrams, the signature index, the per-appliance SSH password and template bindings).
  • No new scheduled actions. The scheduled-action catalogue is the same as in 3.0, so you do not need to run the seed command again.
  • Close data/ right after the upgrade. The update that brings 3.1 closes the vault and bundle directories when they are next used, and data/ itself only on the following update. To apply it at once, run sudo satom execute repair data --yes, then check with satom diagnose data.
  • Set LINK_HOSTS if users reach SATOM under a public alias. Without it, password-reset links point at the node's own name.
  • Choose a signature source under Administrator → Signatures if you have FortiWebs. Without one, an alert says so, and a signature_sync action aimed at another device is refused.
  • Harvest unmeasured builds before applying templates. A target build with no evidence now blocks a template apply. Use Schema builds.
  • Import a current knowledge pack on air-gapped nodes. GUI layouts come only from knowledge packs. Without one, the device ADOMs have no measured pages.
  • If you deploy by git pull instead of the updater, finish with satom execute restart-all so that every service (including the scheduler) runs the new code and the language catalogues are compiled. The new stale-code alert tells you if a process was missed.
  • If you used Settings → FAZ Menu, set the equivalent switches in Settings → ADOM Menus after the upgrade.

SATOM 3.0.0SATOM stops reading Fortinet's website itself and gets its vendor knowledge from signed knowledge packs, warns when a FortiWeb's signature database goes stale, and adds a read-only FortiGate workspace.Architecture (drawn network diagrams)Draw the network path of a service, bind each device element to its SATOM appliance, and read it live by layer (L2, L3, L4, L7). FortiGate interfaces and policies with hit counters are drawn segment to segment, back-ends answer an HTTP probe, and a flow trace asks every FortiGate on the way for its own verdict.Service Diagram (fleet map)An interactive network diagram of the fleet built from SATOM's cache — Internet → published services (VIP:port) → appliance → server pools → back-end servers — with search, filters, a grouped list, device cards and per-policy detail.Not in GUI, but in CLISATOM shows every field and object a device has on its exact build; whatever the Fortinet GUI does not draw is listed under "Not in GUI, but in CLI" — per object in every editor, and per device on one page with the objects the GUI never reads and their rows.Naming scheme and discoveryOne list of object types per product — every table the device sync reads — with the name pattern of each (the FortiWeb entries are how SATOM names what it creates), and Discovery, which reads the names already on the devices, shows the convention behind them and lets you adopt it as found or adapt it first.ADOM Menus settingsThree switches that take the pages SATOM does not draw as configuration (live monitors, pages managed on the device, GUI-only pages with no API) out of the device menu and the All pages list of every ADOM, for every user; a direct link still opens them.FortiAnalyzer workspaceThe FortiAnalyzer ADOM draws the unit's own GUI pages from the layout measured on its build, reads them live over JSON-RPC, writes only /cli/global configuration objects (dry run first, read back and verified), and links monitor and device-managed pages to the unit.API library and API packsThe API library is SATOM's database record of which endpoints and fields each exact firmware build serves, by REST and by CLI; signed API packs and knowledge packs — two lanes, each with its own key — carry that knowledge to nodes that cannot measure it themselves.Operator CLI (satom)The satom command-line console for the node itself — read state, run diagnostics and perform privileged repairs, updates and recoveries, even when the web interface is down.Languages settingsChoose which of SATOM's five interface languages users of this installation may pick; English, the source language, is always offered.
